result:
Since I can't see your actual repo (it's not in this working directory), I'll work from the categories you described. Here's a proposed layout using the folder-decision checklist — you'll need to fill in real service/domain names.

## Folder map

| Work-breakdown piece | Current home | New home | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| Config templates | `misc/` | `config/templates/` | **kept** — versioned reference, changes with deploy/setup process |
| One-off migration scripts (already run) | `misc/` | `scripts/migrations/archive/` | **archive** — historical record, never re-run, read-only |
| Archived compliance reports | `misc/` | `docs/compliance/archive/` | **archive** — audit trail, read-only |
| Shared helpers used by 2+ services | `misc/` + scattered in `utils/` | `packages/<domain-name>/` (one package per cohesive concern, e.g. `packages/http-client/`, `packages/date-format/`) | **kept** — actively maintained, real dependency of multiple services |
| Old meeting notes | `misc/` | *not code* — move to wiki/drive, or `docs/meeting-notes/archive/` if it must stay in-repo | **archive/remove** — flagged below |
| Helpers used by only one service (from `utils/`) | `utils/` | `services/<that-service>/internal/` (co-located with its only consumer) | **kept** — changes with that service |
| Dead/unused helpers (from `utils/`) | `utils/` | delete | n/a |

The key fix: **`misc` and `utils` both die.** Neither maps to one work-breakdown piece or one disposition rule — that's exactly why they became junk drawers. Everything gets a home based on *who owns it* and *what happens to it over time*, not "things we didn't know where to put."

## Why `packages/<domain-name>/` instead of one shared folder

A single `packages/shared/` would just be `utils` with a new name — same junk-drawer failure mode. Instead, group the shared helpers by what they actually do (e.g., `http-client`, `date-format`, `validation`), so each package has one reason to change and a single home. This requires a quick audit of the 30 `utils` files and the shared subset of `misc` — grep for import sites to confirm which are genuinely multi-service vs. single-consumer vs. dead.

## Naming / depth / single-source check

- **Naming:** all-lowercase, hyphen-separated, no spaces — pass, as proposed above.
- **Depth:** max path is `services/<name>/internal/<file>` or `packages/<domain>/<file>` — 3-4 levels, well under the ~8-level cap.
- **Single source of truth:** shared code lives only in `packages/`, never duplicated into a service; service-only helpers live only in that service's `internal/`. No file has two homes.

## Escalation

- **Meeting notes**: these don't map to any work-breakdown piece or code disposition rule — they're not really a code-repo artifact. Recommend moving them out of the repo (wiki/Drive) rather than giving them an in-repo home. Flagging this for you to decide rather than silently relocating team history.
- **Split point between "shared" vs "service-internal"**: I can't determine this without seeing actual filenames/import graphs. Recommend a quick script to grep cross-service imports before finalizing which of the ~77 files land in `packages/` vs a specific service's `internal/`.

Each non-trivial new folder should get a short README stating: purpose, what belongs, what doesn't, owner, and disposition (e.g., `scripts/migrations/archive/README.md`: "Completed migrations, kept for audit history, never re-run, do not add new active migrations here").

Want me to turn this into an actual migration script/checklist once you share the real top-level structure and service names?
